title: KV slotting reservoir: predictive GPU memory orchestration for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As continuous batching and KV-heavy chat workloads scale, we see sporadic OOMs and conservative static reservations that reduce effective throughput. Current heuristics treat weights, KV cache, and activation memory largely independently, which leads to either wasted reserved headroom or tail OOMs under spiky request patterns.

Objective: Implement a predictive "slotting reservoir" memory orchestration layer that dynamically budgets GPU memory across three compartments: model weights (static footprint), KV cache (dynamic but cacheable), and activations (ephemeral, peaked by inflight token concurrency). The system should: 1) maintain safe headroom for tail spikes, 2) maximize usable KV capacity for cache hit improvements, and 3) allow continuous batching to expand throughput without causing OOMs.

Design overview:
- Runtime sensors: expose live metrics (inflight request count, median/95/99 sequence length, avg tokens/sec, per-model KV hit ratio) and a lightweight forecast of short-window (1s-30s) demand percentiles. These sensors feed the slotting reservoir.
- Predictive water-filling allocator: compute a target allocation vector [weights_fixed, kv_target, activations_headroom] per-GPU using a probability-weighted demand forecast. We treat weights as baseline constant; KV and activations are budgeted from the remaining pool. The allocator incorporates a configurable risk-tolerance percentile (default 99th) to size activation headroom.
- Soft reservations + preemption policy: implement soft reservations for activations (fast reclaim) and KV entries (LRU-evict score augmented with utility heuristics). On pressure, the reservoir will (a) throttle batch growth for new requests, (b) evict low-utility KV entries, and (c) temporarily refuse very-large prefix caching for non-critical customers.
- Continuous batching integration: the batcher asks a batch-growth oracle which consults the reservoir to decide whether to accept a larger batch. The oracle returns an allow/deny plus an expected tail-latency impact estimate.
- Memory accounting ledger: unified per-GPU ledger that records committed allocations (weights reserved, kv committed size, activation soft-reserve) and live peak samples for post-hoc billing and telemetry.

Trade-offs & alternatives considered:
- Option A: Fully conservative static reservation per-tenant. Simple but wastes memory in steady state and reduces KV effectiveness.
- Option B: Aggressive eviction-first KV policy. Improves throughput at cost of increasing cache churn and potential quality regressions.
- Chosen: Predictive slotting with a conservative risk percentile and a configurable customer tier policy (enterprise tenants can request higher guaranteed headroom).

Metrics and success criteria:
- Reduce OOM events by >= 90% in production stress tests vs current baseline.
- Increase effective KV usable memory (measured as steady-state occupied KV before eviction) by >= 25% without increasing OOMs.
- Tail latency p95/p99 increases < 10% for steady workloads; throughput (tokens/sec/GPU) improves or remains flat under mixed load.
- New telemetry: "reservoir_utilization" and "kv_eviction_rate" available per-GPU in Console dashboards.

Implementation plan (phased):
1) Simulation & offline tuning (2 weeks): build a replay-based simulator using real traffic traces to validate allocator heuristics and risk percentiles. Produce config knobs.
2) Prototype in runtime (3 weeks): add reservoir module, sensors, and a conservative oracle for batcher integration. Start with soft-only enforcements (no hard preemption).
3) Canary (2 weeks): ship to limited Dedicated pool, monitor OOMs, kv_eviction_rate, tail latency. Adjust percentiles and eviction heuristics.
4) Gradual rollout & optimizations (2-4 weeks): add fast reclaim paths in allocator, integrate tenant-tier policies, expose UI controls in Console (per-model headroom target).

comments: 2025-02-12 | Aisha Patel: Created ticket and uploaded initial design doc. Marking P0 due to customer reports of sporadic OOM on LLM-chat workloads.

2025-02-18 | Marco Hernandez: Completed simulator harness and ran first replay. Observed that naive 95th percentile headroom underestimates 99th tail for bursty traffic — raising default to 99th for initial canary.
2025-02-25 | Priya Rao (SRE): Reviewed ledger/accounting schema. Requested that all reservoir actions emit structured events to central tracing for incident debugging.

2025-03-01 | Marco Hernandez: Prototype module merged to feature branch. Batcher oracle integrated behind feature flag. Basic metrics emitted: reservoir_utilization, kv_eviction_rate, predicted_headroom_pct.

2025-03-05 | Design review notes (Evan Li): Add tenant-tier override and per-model min_kv_quota to avoid starving high-value customers. Also add a fallback to quantized weight variant during severe pressure. Action: Marco to implement quota gating.
2025-03-08 | Marco Hernandez: Canary scheduled for 2025-03-10 on shard-dedicated-phi. Blocking: infra change for faster GPU-reclaim hooks (ENG-33955) — created dependency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No regressions in baseline LTS tests. 2) In canary cohort, OOMs reduced by >=90% in synthetic spike tests. 3) Console shows reservoir metrics and tenant-tier controls. 4) Runbook updated with eviction explanations and mitigation steps.
notes: Edge case: for very large multi-turn contexts (>64k tokens) we may need to fall back to disk-backed spill for activations or reject with a clear 413-like error. Need to coordinate with Private deployment teams to ensure HSM/KMS interactions are unaffected.
